snake-removal.intro: Tatum is a small Marlboro County community near the North Carolina line — flat Pee Dee farm country of fields, pine woods, and swamp branches running to the Little Pee Dee, with a scatter of farmhouses and older rural homes. Its snake work is the Pee Dee rural standard: rat snakes and racers around the barns and houses, watersnakes in the branches and pond edges, and two venomous residents to know — copperheads in the wooded edges and woodpiles, and, in the wettest ground near the swamps, cottonmouths. Tatum's calls are farm calls: a snake in the feed room, a copperhead at the woodpile, a big snake by the pond that turns out, on the photograph, to be a watersnake earning its keep.
snake-removal.extendedBody:
Pee Dee triage: photograph, identify, then act

Tatum work runs on identification discipline. The community's harmless majority — rat snakes in the barns, racers in the yards, watersnakes at the ponds — is genuinely useful and genuinely protected by our advice: we will talk a farmer out of removing his own rodent control unless it is inside the house. The venomous minority is handled at the house ground: a copperhead denning at the woodpile or the steps, a cottonmouth established at a family pond — those are removals, quoted from the photograph before we drive. The habitat read comes with every visit: woodpiles re-sited off the ground and away from doors, brush lines cut back from the buildings, feed stored sealed — the changes that move the seams away from the household's daily paths. In flat farm country the snakes concentrate where the cover meets the work, and moving that meeting line a dozen yards is most of what prevention ever accomplishes, here or anywhere.

faqs.q: How much does snake removal cost in Tatum?
faqs.a: It depends on the species and whether it must be found or simply collected — and it starts, free, with identification from a photograph taken at a safe distance. A share of Tatum's calls end there, with a useful snake named and left on duty. For a removal we quote before we come, and the visit includes the farm walk — woodpiles, feed storage, brush lines — because the snake at the door is the symptom and the seams are the cause.

faqs.q: There is a large snake living in our Tatum barn. Should it be removed?
faqs.a: Send a photograph first. If it is a rat snake, as barn snakes here almost always are, our honest counsel is to keep it: a resident rat snake is continuous, free rodent control, and barns that keep one have fewer rats in the feed and less damage in the wiring. The exceptions: a snake inside the house itself, one in a space where small children work daily, or a venomous species misidentified — the photo settles which case you have. If removal is right, we do it and show you the rodent sign the snake was living on, because that is the problem that remains.
